re_line: Beijing's market rescue · USTR's new 301 tariffs on 14 economies · Taiwan votes amid PLA activity · Nvidia's SE Asia halt
morning_memo: China's State Council issued a rare midday statement pledging stronger 'national team' intervention in capital markets, sending the CSI 300 to its biggest one-day gain in two years and the SSE Composite up 1.91 percent.

USTR published results of its Section 301 'structural overcapacity' investigation on Nov 25, proposing new tariffs on 14 economies including China; Beijing's state trade promotion body urged Washington to withdraw the measure.

Taiwan heads into Saturday's nine-in-one local elections after Reuters reported China sent warplanes as campaigning entered its final day, with China-sanctioned DPP Taipei candidate Puma Shen emerging as a serious challenger to KMT incumbent Chiang Wan-an.

key_stat.label: Decline in Chinese household consumption debt, Jan-Oct 2026
key_stat.context: PBOC data cited by FT Chinese show total household consumption loans, including mortgages, fell to ¥56.6 trillion ($8.5 trillion), more than three times the ¥500 billion full-year decline recorded in 2025.

prc_government.action: Issued new rules on RMB deposit and loan interest rate management
prc_government.document: 《人民币存贷款利率管理规定》(Provisions on the Administration of RMB Deposit and Loan Interest Rates)
prc_government.detail: The regulation, approved Oct 30 2026 at the PBOC's 10th executive meeting, takes effect March 21 2027 and lowers minimum large-denomination certificate of deposit subscriptions to ¥100,000 for individuals and ¥5 million for institutions.

prc_government.action: Chaired executive meeting on capital markets and standards reform
prc_government.detail: The Nov 27 meeting called for a greater 'national team' investor role, an enhanced quasi-stabilization function for Central Huijin, and crackdowns on financial fraud and illegal share reductions; it also reviewed a draft workplace-safety hazard rule.

prc_government.action: Completed second China-Vietnam coast guard joint patrol of Gulf of Tonkin in 2026
prc_government.detail: China's and Vietnam's coast guards concluded their second joint patrol of the Gulf of Tonkin this year, per MND, part of routine bilateral maritime cooperation.

calendar_watch.headline: Taiwan nine-in-one local elections
calendar_watch.detail: 22 mayors and magistrates and roughly 11,000 offices are at stake; the Taipei mayoral race between KMT incumbent Chiang Wan-an and DPP's Puma Shen is watched as a mid-term test for President Lai Ching-te.

calendar_watch.headline: Philippine Senate impeachment court resumes Sara Duterte trial
calendar_watch.detail: The Senate impeachment court reconvenes for the final phase of proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte, who says she will not resign.

calendar_watch.headline: Nanjing Massacre National Memorial Day
calendar_watch.detail: China's annual state commemoration (国家公祭日) of the 1937 Nanjing Massacre.

calendar_watch.headline: G20 Leaders' Summit, Doral (Miami)
calendar_watch.detail: The US hosts the G20 summit Dec 14-15; Xi Jinping's attendance has not been confirmed.

calendar_watch.headline: Trump-Xi trade truce reportedly set to expire
calendar_watch.detail: Per BBC Chinese, the 20 percent US tariff rate on China, matched to the Trump-Xi trade truce, is reported to expire in mid-January 2027.

overnight_items.headline: Toyota Car Sales Fall for Ninth Straight Month as China Slump Worsens
overnight_items.body_text: Toyota's China sales fell for a ninth consecutive month, Bloomberg reports, as the broader slowdown in China's auto market deepens further. The decline adds pressure on legacy automakers already losing ground to Chinese EV makers in their home market.

overnight_items.headline: Former Guangxi Government Chief Sentenced to Death With Reprieve for Graft
overnight_items.body_text: A former government chief of China's Guangxi region was sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve on corruption charges, Reuters reports. Such suspended sentences are commonly commuted to life imprisonment after a period of good behavior.

overnight_items.headline: Fall of Shanghai Party Chief Clouds China's 2027 Leadership Reset
overnight_items.body_text: Beijing's announcement that Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining is under investigation has cast a shadow over China's planned 2027 leadership transition, per Nikkei. Jamestown separately frames the move as ending the political influence of the so-called Tsinghua clique.

overnight_items.headline: Hong Kong Fire Survivors Mark Anniversary as Accountability Questions Linger
overnight_items.body_text: Survivors and families marked one year since the Wang Fuk Court fire killed 168 people, Hong Kong's deadliest blaze in decades, per Nikkei. No official government commemoration was held, and questions over responsibility remain unresolved.

overnight_items.headline: China's Sany Pushes AI Into Heavy Machinery as Overseas Sales Grow
overnight_items.body_text: Sany Heavy Industry plans to roll out autonomous mining equipment and AI agents capable of coordinating entire equipment fleets, Nikkei reports. The push comes as the company's overseas sales continue to expand.

overnight_items.headline: TSMC-Backed European Semiconductor Manufacturing to Begin Production Late 2027
overnight_items.body_text: European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, backed by TSMC, is on track to begin production in late 2027, per Taiwan News. The plant forms part of Europe's push to diversify chipmaking capacity away from Asia.

overnight_items.headline: Singapore Wealth Firm Farro Plans Hong Kong Office With 20 Hires
overnight_items.body_text: Singapore-based wealth manager Farro plans to open a Hong Kong office and hire 20 staff, Bloomberg reports. The move reflects continuing interest in the city's family-office and wealth-management sector.

overnight_items.headline: China's Super-Rich Chase Million-Dollar Koi Amid Wealth Crackdown
overnight_items.body_text: Chinese collectors are paying fortunes for prized koi fish even as an economic slowdown and Beijing's crackdown on conspicuous wealth threaten the market, per FT. Prices for top specimens have reached seven figures.

us_china.headline: Nvidia GPU Buyers Told to Exclude Chinese Renters Under New BIS Rule
us_china.body_text: Neocloud operators have been instructed to rule out Chinese renters before purchasing Nvidia GPUs, sources told CNBC, after a new BIS rule intended to close export-control 'loopholes.' USTR **Jamieson Greer** said the rule targets indirect Chinese access to advanced AI chips via rented cloud capacity.

us_china.headline: China's Trade Body Urges US to Withdraw Proposed 301 Tariffs
us_china.body_text: The China Council for the Promotion of International Trade said Chinese business circles 'resolutely oppose' USTR's Nov 25 proposal to impose new Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, including China, over alleged manufacturing overcapacity. CCTV reported the group called on Washington to withdraw the measure.

us_china.headline: BBC Chinese: New Tariff Threat Lands Softer Than 2025's 'Liberation Day'
us_china.body_text: BBC Chinese reports the new duties will not take effect until January or February 2027 after an eight-month consultation, in contrast to last year's overnight 'Liberation Day' shock. The 20 percent China rate matches the Trump-Xi trade truce level, reported due to expire in mid-January; 25 US states are separately suing to overturn earlier forced-labor-based tariffs.

us_china.headline: Asian Governments Reject Basis of New Trump Tariffs, Nikkei Reports
us_china.body_text: Asian governments hit by the new overcapacity-based tariffs are disputing Washington's rationale even as the US compiles what Nikkei describes as additional 'ammunition' against China. The duties stem from USTR's Nov 25 findings covering 14 named economies.

us_china.source: 人民日报国际 (People's Daily World ZH)
us_china.headline: Dutch Officials Oppose US Push to Tighten Chip-Equipment Export Controls
us_china.body_text: Dutch officials said they oppose proposed US legislation that would strengthen export controls on semiconductor manufacturing equipment, per People's Daily's international desk. The brief report did not specify the bill's sponsor or its status in Congress.

china_world.headline: Chinese Military Tests New Taiwan Landing Tactics in Coastal Drills
china_world.body_text: The Chinese military has tested new amphibious landing tactics during coastal drills oriented toward a Taiwan contingency, the Japan Times reports. The drills precede Taiwan's Nov 28 local elections amid heightened cross-strait tension.

china_world.headline: Sanctioned China Critic Puma Shen Could Become Taipei's Next Mayor
china_world.body_text: **Puma Shen**, sanctioned by Beijing for organizing civilian invasion-preparedness efforts, could become Taiwan's next political star if he wins Saturday's Taipei mayoral race, per NYT. He faces KMT incumbent Chiang Wan-an in a contest watched as a bellwether for 2028.

china_world.headline: Taiwan Secures Preferential Tariff Treatment for Chipmakers Ahead of US Section 232 Rate
china_world.body_text: Vice Premier **Cheng Li-chiun** said Taiwan has negotiated exemptions from potential US semiconductor tariffs within agreed quotas and a non-stacked rate of no more than 15 percent, under a January investment memorandum. The remarks followed Washington's Nov 25 proposal to impose Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, including Taiwan, over alleged overcapacity.

china_world.headline: Lithuania Threatens to Revoke Taiwan Office's Legal Status
china_world.body_text: Lithuanian President **Gitanas Nauseda** said the government could unilaterally revoke the legal status of Taiwan's representative office in Vilnius if Taipei refuses to drop 'Taiwanese' from its name. The dispute dates to the office's November 2021 opening, which prompted Beijing to downgrade diplomatic relations with Lithuania.

china_world.headline: Nissan to Import China-Made Plug-In Hybrids to Japan for First Time
china_world.body_text: Nissan is preparing to sell in Japan plug-in hybrids built by a joint venture in China, taking advantage of faster development and lower production costs, per Nikkei. It would mark the first time Nissan imports China-made vehicles into the Japanese market.

china_world.headline: China, Russia Militaries Hold Strategic Consultations by Video Link
china_world.body_text: China's and Russia's defense ministries held strategic consultations via video conference on Nov 26, exchanging views on implementing the two heads of state's consensus and deepening military ties, per China's Defense Ministry. Russia's deputy defense minister Osmakov took part in what Russian state media called the first round of such consultations.

china_world.headline: Chinese Think Tank: US Rebuilding Subic Bay as 'Unbranded Military Base'
china_world.body_text: A report from the National Institute for South China Sea Studies says the US is rebuilding a network of facilities at Subic Bay in the Philippines, logistics, fuel storage, ship repair and weapons stockpiles, that could support operations in both the South China Sea and the Taiwan Strait. The report was released Wednesday, per SCMP.

china_world.headline: China Railway Resources Group to Invest $600 Million in Zimbabwe Gold Mines
china_world.body_text: China Railway Resources Group plans a *$600 million* investment in Zimbabwe's gold mining sector, Reuters reports. The investment adds to China's existing mining footprint in the country, which includes lithium and platinum operations.

top_stories.headline: Taiwan's Election Eve: China Sends Warplanes as Sanctioned DPP Candidate Surges in Taipei
top_stories.body: Taiwan's nine-in-one local elections take place Nov 28, electing 22 mayors and magistrates; Reuters reports China sent warplanes as campaigning entered its final day. DPP legislator **Puma Shen**, sanctioned by Beijing for civil-defense preparation work, has emerged as a serious Taipei mayoral contender against KMT incumbent Chiang Wan-an, per NYT.

top_stories.headline: USTR Proposes New Section 301 Tariffs on 14 Economies Including China
top_stories.body: The US Trade Representative published findings Nov 25 from its 'structural excess capacity' Section 301 investigation, proposing new tariffs on 14 economies including China, per AP. China's state trade promotion body CCPIT said business circles 'resolutely oppose' the move and called for the measures to be withdrawn, per CCTV.

top_stories.headline: Beijing's Rare Midday Market-Support Statement Fuels Biggest Rally in Two Years
top_stories.body: China's State Council issued a rare midday statement pledging to deepen capital market reforms, sending the CSI 300 to its biggest one-day rise in two years and lifting the SSE Composite *1.91 percent* and the Hang Seng *1.27 percent*. Premier **Li Qiang** chaired the State Council's Nov 27 executive meeting, which called for greater 'national team' investor support and an enhanced quasi-stabilization role for Central Huijin, per Xinhua.

top_stories.headline: Nvidia Halts Chip Shipments to Southeast Asia Under New BIS Licensing Rule
top_stories.body: Nvidia told partners Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping AI servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after a new Commerce Department rule requiring licenses for advanced chips destined for the region, per NYT. Chinese state media separately noted Nvidia's Singapore subsidiary alone recorded *$104 billion* in 2025 revenue, up 72 percent year-on-year.

top_stories.headline: China, Japan Trade Accusations Over Senkaku/Diaoyu Intrusion
top_stories.body: Japan's coast guard said it repeatedly warned two Chinese vessels approaching a Japanese fishing boat near the Senkaku/Diaoyu islands on Nov 26, the fifth such incident this year. **Guo Jiakun** of China's Foreign Ministry said China 'lodged serious representations' with Japan and that coast guard vessels 'took necessary control measures... in accordance with the law.'

also_today.headline: A Game-Changing Move Just Gave America the Edge Over China in AI
also_today.body_text: WSJ reports a policy shift has strengthened the US position in the AI race against China.

also_today.headline: Chinese Cities Want to Become 'Token Factories' for the World
also_today.body_text: The Economist reports Chinese cities are competing to host AI compute infrastructure serving global demand.

also_today.headline: China Hedge Fund Star Builds Operating System Kernel for AI
also_today.body_text: A prominent Chinese hedge fund manager is developing an AI operating-system kernel, Bloomberg reports.

also_today.headline: China Tech's Earnings Offer Little Relief in Worst-Ever Year
also_today.body_text: Chinese tech companies' latest earnings have failed to reverse what Bloomberg calls their worst year on record.

also_today.headline: Taiwan Machinery Makers See Limited Impact From Proposed US Tariffs
also_today.body_text: Focus Taiwan reports local machinery makers expect minimal disruption from Washington's newly proposed Section 301 tariffs.

also_today.headline: Taiwan Elections: Five Things to Know About Races Eyed by China and US
also_today.body_text: Nikkei outlines the city and county races in Saturday's vote that Beijing and Washington are watching most closely.

also_today.headline: Mistranslated Clip Falsely Shared as Trump Criticizing Taiwan President
also_today.body_text: AFP Fact Check debunks a viral clip misrepresenting Trump as criticizing Lai Ching-te ahead of Saturday's local polls.

also_today.headline: Taiwan Weathers Wave of Cyberattacks Ahead of Saturday's Elections
also_today.body_text: Nikkei reports a barrage of cyberattacks has targeted Taiwanese officials and politicians in the run-up to Saturday's vote.

business_economy.headline: China's Industrial Profit Growth Fastest in Five Months
business_economy.body_text: China's industrial profits rose 1.6 percent year-on-year in the January-October period, the fastest pace in five months, though the recovery remains uneven.

business_economy.headline: Chinese Chip Stocks Post Biggest-Ever One-Day Gains
business_economy.body_text: Chinese semiconductor stocks notched their biggest one-day gains on record after a rare intraday state media readout and top policymaker pledges of market liquidity support, per CNBC.

business_economy.headline: Stellantis to Pause More Europe Plants as Chinese Rivals Advance
business_economy.body_text: Stellantis is set to pause additional European production lines as Chinese automakers expand their market share, Bloomberg reports.

business_economy.headline: Rest of World Plays Catch-Up With China's Solar Power Dominance
business_economy.body_text: Europe, India and the US are investing in domestic solar and battery manufacturing but remain far from reducing reliance on Chinese suppliers, per FT.

business_economy.headline: China's Wind Turbine Makers Expand Abroad Amid Domestic Pressure
business_economy.body_text: Chinese wind turbine manufacturers are expanding into emerging markets as intense domestic competition and political barriers limit growth in the West, per FT.

business_economy.headline: Hong Kong Seeks to Lure Sovereign Wealth Funds With Tax Breaks
business_economy.body_text: Hong Kong is offering tax incentives to attract sovereign wealth funds after some global investors pulled out or scaled back teams in the financial hub, per FT.

official_line.speaker: Guo Jiakun
official_line.topic: Senkaku/Diaoyu waters intrusion dispute with Japan
official_line.statement: China has already lodged serious representations with Japan. Chinese coast guard vessels took necessary control measures against the relevant vessels in accordance with the law.
official_line.context: Japan's coast guard said it warned two Chinese vessels approaching a Japanese fishing boat near the Senkaku/Diaoyu islands on Nov 26, the fifth such incident this year.

official_line.speaker: MOFA spokesperson
official_line.topic: Response to new US tariffs on Chinese goods
official_line.statement: Per Eastmoney: Both sides should jointly implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state.
official_line.context: USTR proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies including China on Nov 25, citing 'structural overcapacity.'

official_line.speaker: Zhang Han
official_line.topic: Other countries' affirmation of the one-China principle at APEC
official_line.statement: Per Tencent News: multiple countries' leaders affirmed the one-China principle during the APEC summit, and 'we appreciate the position of the relevant countries,' TAO spokesperson Zhang Han said on Nov 25.
official_line.original_zh: 在APEC会议期间，多国领导人明确表示，坚定恪守一个中国原则，国台办发言人张晗25日表示，我们对有关国家的立场表示赞赏
official_line.context: The remark followed multiple APEC-attending leaders reaffirming the one-China principle during the Nov 2026 summit.

official_line.speaker: Li Qiang
official_line.statement: Per Xinhua (State Council readout): the meeting called for resolutely investigating financial fraud and illegal share reductions, effectively protecting investors' legitimate rights, and strengthening the 'national team's' market-stabilizing role.
official_line.original_zh: 坚决查处财务造假、违规减持等行为，有效保护投资者合法权益...加力发挥'国家队'稳市作用
official_line.context: Li Qiang chaired the State Council executive meeting on Nov 27, which also discussed optimizing Central Huijin's quasi-stabilization-fund function.

social_statements.quote_text: We expect wide-ranging, even multilateral, negotiations on the overcapacity issue and how to resolve it.
social_statements.analyst_note: Greer's comments followed USTR's Nov 25 publication of Section 301 'structural overcapacity' findings proposing tariffs on 14 economies including China.

social_statements.quote_text: actively take action ... to repeal Trump's tariffs
social_statements.analyst_note: Democrats are set to control the House after the Nov 3 2026 midterms; Jeffries made the comment this week per BBC Chinese.

social_statements.quote_text: In the past years there were certain expectations. But the end result was different.
social_statements.analyst_note: Nauseda said the government could unilaterally revoke Taipei's representative office status if Taiwan refuses to drop 'Taiwanese' from the office's name, a dispute dating to its Nov 2021 opening.

personnel_changes.name: Chen Jining
personnel_changes.detail: Nikkei reports Beijing's announcement that Chen Jining is under investigation has cast a shadow over China's 2027 leadership reset; Jamestown separately describes it as marking the end of the 'Tsinghua clique.'
